question: I earn 12 lakh a year, do I have to pay any tax in the new regime?
answer: No tax if total income is up to ₹12,00,000 under the new regime because of the Section 87A rebate (up to ₹60,000). With the ₹75,000 standard deduction, salary up to ₹12,75,000 is tax-free.

question: What are the new tax slabs this year?
How much can I save by investing in PPF and ELSS?
answer: PPF and ELSS count under Section 80C, deduction up to ₹1,50,000 in total, old regime only.

question: I pay rent in Bangalore, how is my HRA exemption calculated?
answer: Exempt HRA is the least of: actual HRA received, rent paid minus 10% of basic+DA, and 40% of basic for non-metro cities (50% for Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai). Old regime only.

question: Can I claim my parents' health insurance premium?
answer: Yes under Section 80D, up to ₹25,000 for parents below 60 or ₹50,000 if a parent is a senior citizen, in addition to the self/family limit. Old regime only.

question: My company puts money in NPS for me, is that tax free?
answer: Employer NPS contribution is deductible under Section 80CCD(2) in both regimes: up to 14% of basic+DA in the new regime; 10% for private employers in the old regime.

question: Is there an extra deduction if I put my own money into NPS?
answer: Section 80CCD(1B) gives an additional ₹50,000 deduction over the ₹1.5 lakh 80C limit, old regime only.

question: How much home loan interest can I deduct for the flat I live in?
answer: Up to ₹2,00,000 a year on a self-occupied house under Section 24(b), old regime only.

question: What is the standard deduction for salaried people?
answer: ₹75,000 under the new regime and ₹50,000 under the old regime (Section 16(ia)).

question: Is the interest from my savings bank account taxable?
answer: It is taxable but Section 80TTA allows a deduction of up to ₹10,000 (old regime); senior citizens get up to ₹50,000 under 80TTB.

question: Can I use ITR-1 if I have two houses?
answer: Yes for AY 2026-27: ITR-1 now allows up to two house properties. More than two requires ITR-2.

question: Who is not allowed to file ITR-1?
answer: Non-residents, people with income above ₹50 lakh, business income, capital gains other than 112A LTCG up to ₹1.25L, more than two house properties, company directors, unlisted shares, foreign assets.

question: What do the different parts of Form 16 mean?
answer: Part A shows employer/employee details and quarterly TDS; Part B shows salary breakup, exemptions, Section 16 deductions, Chapter VI-A deductions and tax computation.

question: I travelled to Goa with family, can I claim LTA?
answer: LTA under Section 10(5) covers domestic travel fare only (not hotel/food), for two journeys in a four-year block, old regime only.

question: Is the money I get when my LIC policy matures taxable?
answer: Maturity proceeds are exempt under Section 10(10D) if premium conditions are met (premium within 10% of sum assured for newer policies; limits apply to high-premium policies).

question: Can I deduct the interest on my education loan?
answer: Yes, Section 80E allows the full interest (no cap) for up to 8 years on a loan for higher education of self, spouse or children; old regime only.

question: Do donations to charity reduce my tax?
answer: Donations to approved funds/institutions qualify under Section 80G at 50% or 100%, sometimes subject to a 10% of income limit; old regime.

question: Which regime is better for me if I have lots of deductions?
answer: The old regime can be better only with large deductions (80C, 80D, HRA, home-loan interest); compare both. Under the new slabs the break-even is high.

question: My income is 12.1 lakh, will I lose the whole rebate?
answer: No — marginal relief caps tax at the excess over ₹12 lakh, so tax is ₹10,000 (+cess) rather than ₹61,500.

question: What counts as salary for income tax?
answer: Section 15: salary due or paid by an employer, including arrears and advance salary, is chargeable under the head Salaries.

question: Is professional tax deductible?
answer: Professional tax is deductible under Section 16(iii) in the old regime only; the new regime allows only the standard deduction.

question: Is there any tax relief on my foreign retirement account?
answer: Section 89A lets residents defer tax on income accrued in a retirement account maintained in a notified country; it is not available in ITR-1 for AY 2026-27.

question: What is the last date to file my return this year?
answer: 31 July 2026 for AY 2026-27 without audit; belated return up to 31 December 2026 with late fee.

question: Can I claim HRA if I live in my own house?
answer: No — HRA exemption requires actually paying rent and not owning a house in the same city.

question: Do I need my landlord's PAN for HRA?
answer: Yes if annual rent exceeds ₹1,00,000 (about ₹8,333 a month), the landlord's PAN must be given to the employer.

question: Does the home loan principal count for tax saving?
answer: Home loan principal repayment is part of Section 80C within the ₹1.5 lakh limit, old regime.

question: My father is 65, how much health insurance can I deduct for him?
answer: Up to ₹50,000 under Section 80D because he is a senior citizen.

question: I am a senior citizen, how much FD interest is tax free?
answer: Section 80TTB allows senior citizens a deduction of up to ₹50,000 on interest from savings and deposits (old regime).

question: Is health and education cess charged on top of tax?
answer: Yes, 4% cess on income tax plus surcharge.

question: Can I switch between old and new regime every year?
answer: Salaried individuals without business income can choose either regime every year when filing; new regime is the default.

question: How is tax on stock market gains handled with the 87A rebate?
answer: The 87A rebate is not available against special-rate tax on capital gains (Sections 111A/112/112A).

question: What is the maximum I can claim under 80C, 80CCC and 80CCD(1) together?
answer: Section 80CCE caps 80C + 80CCC + 80CCD(1) together at ₹1,50,000.

question: Can I claim interest on a house that is still under construction?
answer: Pre-construction interest is deductible in five equal instalments starting from the year construction completes, within the ₹2 lakh limit for self-occupied property.

question: What tax-free allowances are shown in Form 16?
answer: Allowances exempt under Section 10 such as HRA (10(13A)) and LTA (10(5)) appear separately in Part B before net salary.

question: Is a children's tuition fee eligible for tax saving?
answer: Tuition fees for up to two children qualify under Section 80C within the ₹1.5 lakh limit.

question: What is the surcharge in the new regime for very high income?
answer: Surcharge is capped at 25% in the new regime (10% above ₹50L, 15% above ₹1Cr, 25% above ₹2Cr).

question: What is the basic exemption limit under the old regime?
If my rent is paid to my mother can I still get HRA?
answer: Yes, if the rent is actually paid and the parent declares it as rental income.

question: Does preventive health check-up count for 80D?
answer: Yes, up to ₹5,000 for preventive health check-ups within the overall 80D limit.

question: How many times can I claim LTA in four years?
answer: Two journeys in a block of four calendar years.

question: Section 87A rebate limit under section 115BAC new regime
answer: Rebate up to ₹60,000 for total income up to ₹12,00,000 (AY 2026-27).

question: Rule 2A computation of exempt house rent allowance
answer: Least of actual HRA, rent minus 10% of salary, 50%/40% of salary.

question: Section 80CCD(2) employer contribution limit
answer: 14% of salary (new regime / government); 10% for other employers in old regime.

question: Section 24(b) interest on borrowed capital self-occupied property
Section 16(ia) standard deduction
answer: ₹50,000 old regime, ₹75,000 new regime.

question: Section 80TTB deduction senior citizen interest
Section 10(10D) sum received under life insurance policy
answer: Exempt subject to premium-to-sum-assured and high-premium conditions.

question: ITR-1 Schedule VI-A deductions
answer: Chapter VI-A deductions such as 80C, 80CCD, 80D, 80E, 80G, 80TTA are reported in Schedule VI-A.

question: Section 80E interest on loan for higher education deduction period
answer: Up to 8 assessment years from the year repayment starts.

question: Section 115BAC(1A) slab rates Finance Act 2025
